newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks close sharply down on selling rush.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks close sharply down on selling rush.

text.p: Selling pressure prompted by a general strike planned for Tuesday, continuing floods and changes in the Securities and Exchange Commission pushed prices at the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) sharply lower on Monday, brokers said.
The DSE all-share index dropped 35.86 points or 3.47 percent at 996.5 on a turnover of 36.2 million taka. Only five out of 116 shares traded recorded gains.
Bangladesh Lamps lost 188 taka to 4,545 and Chittagong Cement Clinker shed 164 taka to 1,650.
"The market sentiment was very weak after appointment of Mohammad Abu Sayeed on Sunday as new chief in the SEC, the market watchdog, following resignation of Harunur Rashid," one broker said.
"Rashid initiated a number of steps to reform the market which has been rocked by price manipulation and other irregularities," he said.
Investors were also nervous because of the continuing floods causing property and crop damage, and over the strike called by radical Islamic groups in Bangladesh.
The Islamic groups say the Prophet Mohammad was defamed when a right wing Jewish woman in the west bank town of Hebron plastered storefronts with posters protraying Mohammed as a pig.
